checklistGeneric: Confirm the risk assessment methodology was applied consistently
Confirm the assessment output was reviewed by a second reviewer
checklistSpecific: Score each identified vulnerability against the business service's approved impact tolerance metric (duration, data loss, financial, customer harm)
Flag any vulnerability where projected disruption exceeds the impact tolerance threshold as a tolerance breach in the resilience vulnerability register
Record the assumptions and scenario parameters used in the assessment against the vulnerability record
Attach the impact tolerance breach rationale to the corresponding important business service entry in Archer GRC
Route tolerance-breach vulnerabilities to the Operational Resilience Lead for prioritisation review

testing.expected: Each vulnerability record shows an impact tolerance score and breach flag where applicable

checklistGeneric: Confirm each remediation action has a named accountable owner
Confirm the plan is stored against the correct vulnerability register entry
checklistSpecific: Draft a remediation plan for each tolerance-breach vulnerability naming the accountable action owner, target completion date, and estimated cost
Size the investment ask (headcount, capex, vendor spend) for each remediation option against the vulnerability register entry
Sequence remediation actions by tolerance-breach severity and dependency
Record the remediation plan document reference against the corresponding vulnerability record in Archer GRC
Circulate the draft remediation investment plan to the Business Continuity Manager for feasibility review before submission

testing.location: remediation plan attachment on vulnerability register
testing.expected: Costed remediation plan with owner and target date attached to each tolerance-breach vulnerability

checklistGeneric: Confirm each validation session is logged with attendees and date
Confirm outstanding validations are tracked to closure
checklistSpecific: Schedule validation review sessions with the business unit, technology, and third-party management leads named as vulnerability owners
Walk each management lead through their assigned vulnerability entries and capture their sign-off or dispute in the register
Record any disputed vulnerability findings and the lead's rationale as a comment against the register entry
Update the vulnerability owner field once each lead has confirmed accountability
Confirm outstanding validations are chased to closure within the agreed review window

testing.expected: Each vulnerability entry carries a management lead sign-off or logged dispute

checklistGeneric: Confirm the escalation meets the defined escalation trigger threshold
Confirm the Committee decision is recorded and actioned
checklistSpecific: Identify remediation actions that have missed their committed milestone date by more than the defined escalation threshold
Draft the delay escalation paper naming the overdue remediation, root cause, revised date, and residual risk exposure
Attach the escalation paper to the Board Risk Committee pack in the board portal ahead of the scheduled meeting
Record the Board Risk Committee's decision (accept delay, demand acceleration, reassign owner) against the remediation action in Archer GRC
Update the remediation action's status and revised milestone date following the Committee decision

testing.expected: Delay escalation paper filed with root cause, revised date and Committee decision recorded

checklistGeneric: Confirm the approval decision is captured with date and approver
Confirm the approved plan is filed as supporting evidence
checklistSpecific: Package the remediation investment plan with total cost, prioritised vulnerability list, and expected tolerance impact for senior management sign-off
Route the investment plan to the Chief Risk Officer for approval via the GRC platform's approval workflow
Capture the approver's decision, conditions, and approval date on the investment plan record
Record any approved budget adjustments against the original remediation cost estimate
File the signed approval record against the resilience vulnerability register as supporting evidence

testing.expected: Investment plan shows CRO approval decision, date and any conditions

checklistGeneric: Confirm the approved scoring matrix was used
Confirm the ranked list is published for remediation planning
checklistSpecific: Score each vulnerability on the standard likelihood and severity scale using the approved scoring matrix
Plot scored vulnerabilities on the resilience heat map to visualise priority tiers
Assign each vulnerability a priority tier (Critical/High/Medium/Low) in the vulnerability register
Cross-check tier assignments against prior period scores to flag any material rating changes
Publish the ranked vulnerability list for remediation planning

testing.expected: Every open vulnerability carries a likelihood score, severity score and priority tier

checklistGeneric: Confirm the re-assessment covers every item closed in the prior 12 months
Confirm the annual re-assessment date is recorded
checklistSpecific: Pull the prior-year vulnerability register and re-score each remediated item's residual risk after controls were implemented
Confirm remediation actions closed in the prior 12 months remain effective by re-testing the control
Record the annual re-assessment date and reviewer against each vulnerability record
Reopen any vulnerability where residual risk has drifted back above the impact tolerance threshold
Archive the annual re-assessment summary in the resilience evidence repository

testing.expected: Each closed vulnerability shows an annual residual-risk re-assessment dated within the last 12 months

checklistGeneric: Confirm the service map reviewed is the latest published version
Confirm newly identified vulnerabilities are logged in the register
checklistSpecific: Pull the current service map for each important business service showing people, process, technology and third-party dependencies
Walk the mapped dependency chain end-to-end to identify single points of failure or missing redundancy
Cross-reference third-party dependencies on the service map against the vendor register for concentration risk
Log each newly identified vulnerability as a new entry in the resilience vulnerability register with the source service map reference
Confirm the service map version reviewed matches the latest published version in Confluence

testing.expected: Newly identified vulnerabilities are logged with a service map reference and dependency type

checklistGeneric: Confirm amber/red items are flagged for follow-up
Confirm the dashboard reflects the latest owner-reported status
checklistSpecific: Pull the current status of every open remediation action against its committed milestone date
Flag any remediation action that is amber (within 2 weeks of due date, not started) or red (overdue) on the tracking dashboard
Chase the assigned action owner for an updated status and evidence of progress on amber/red items
Update the milestone tracker with the latest status, percent complete, and revised date where applicable
Publish the remediation progress dashboard for the monthly resilience governance meeting

testing.expected: Every open remediation action shows current status, percent complete and next milestone date

checklistGeneric: Confirm closure evidence is attached before status is changed
Confirm the closed item is removed from the active backlog view
checklistSpecific: Confirm the remediation action's closure evidence (control test result, implementation sign-off) is attached to the vulnerability record
Re-score the vulnerability's residual risk after remediation and update the tier
Change the vulnerability status from Open/In Remediation to Closed once evidence is validated
Record the closure date and validating reviewer on the vulnerability register entry
Confirm the closed vulnerability is removed from the active remediation backlog view

testing.expected: Remediated vulnerability shows Closed status, closure date, reviewer and updated residual risk score

checklistGeneric: Confirm every scored vulnerability without a remediation is captured in the backlog
Confirm the backlog ranking is agreed before publication
checklistSpecific: Pull all vulnerabilities scored in the current period that lack an assigned remediation action
Rank the unscheduled vulnerabilities into the remediation backlog by priority tier and available remediation capacity
Assign a target remediation window (quarter) to each backlog item
Confirm the backlog ranking is reviewed and agreed with the Operational Resilience Lead before publication
Publish the ranked remediation backlog to the resilience governance forum

testing.expected: Every scored vulnerability without a completed remediation appears in the ranked backlog with a target quarter

checklistGeneric: Confirm each control owner responds within the agreed window
Confirm disputed findings are adjudicated before the list is locked
checklistSpecific: Distribute the draft vulnerability findings list to the named control owner for each affected business service
Confirm each control owner has reviewed and either accepted or contested the finding within the response window
Record contested findings with the control owner's rationale and route to the Operational Resilience Lead for adjudication
Confirm remediation accountability is formally assigned to a named owner for each validated finding
Lock the validated findings list before it feeds the prioritisation and backlog step

testing.expected: Every finding shows control owner acceptance or a logged, adjudicated dispute

checklistGeneric: Confirm every mapped dependency is assessed against its service's tolerance
Confirm flagged gaps are handed off for formal logging
checklistSpecific: Pull the mapped dependency list for each important business service from the service map
Model each dependency's plausible disruption duration against the service's approved impact tolerance
Flag dependencies where a plausible disruption scenario would breach the impact tolerance as a resilience gap
Record the gap rationale, affected dependency and disruption scenario against the business service entry
Hand off flagged gaps to the vulnerability identification step for formal logging

testing.expected: Each important business service dependency shows a plausible-disruption assessment against its impact tolerance

checklistGeneric: Confirm every important business service has a named service owner
Confirm disputed thresholds are resolved before finalising
checklistSpecific: Circulate the proposed impact tolerance metric and threshold for each important business service to its named service owner
Capture the service owner's written confirmation or requested adjustment against each tolerance record
Resolve any disputed threshold with the service owner and Enterprise Risk Manager before finalising
Record the confirmation date and confirming service owner against the impact tolerance entry
Lock confirmed impact tolerances as the baseline for the next scenario-testing cycle

testing.expected: Each important business service shows a service-owner-confirmed impact tolerance with confirmation date

checklistGeneric: Confirm the service map covers people, process, technology and third-party layers
Confirm the service owner signs off the completed map
checklistSpecific: List each important business service and its end-to-end delivery chain (people, process, technology, third-party)
Identify the specific applications, facilities, and staffing groups that deliver each business service
Identify the named third-party providers and outsourced arrangements the service depends on, cross-referenced to the vendor register
Publish the completed service map in Confluence and link it from the business service's record in Archer GRC
Confirm the service map has been reviewed and signed off by the business service owner

testing.expected: Each important business service links to a published, owner-approved service map covering people, process, technology and third-party assets

checklistGeneric: Confirm each threshold ties back to the board-approved risk appetite
Confirm the approved tolerances carry an effective date
checklistSpecific: Define the impact tolerance metric (maximum tolerable disruption duration, data loss, customer/financial harm) for each important business service
Set the specific quantitative threshold for each metric based on the risk appetite statement
Draft the impact tolerance paper for Enterprise Risk Manager review before submission to the Chief Risk Officer
Route the proposed impact tolerances through the board approval workflow required for material resilience decisions
Record the approved impact tolerance thresholds in the impact tolerance register with effective date

testing.expected: Each important business service has an approved impact tolerance threshold with effective date and approver recorded
